To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of a BGO calorimeter prototype is good enough to be used as an outer hadron calorimeter of the L3 detector at LEP.
we measured the energy resolution of a BGO calorimeter module to be 29% at 4-GeV, 21% at 10-GeV and 18% at 20-GeV.
we measured the energy resolution of the BGO calorimeter prototype module to be 30% at 6GeV, 21% at 10GeV, and 18% at 20GeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a hadron calorimeter with a BGO absorber.
the development of a calorimeter module for the L3 experiment at the CERN Large Electron-Positron Collider (LEP) and with the measurement of the energy resolution of this calorimeter module.
the construction, the testing, and the performance of a prototype of a gas-sampling uranium module for the L3 hadronic calorimeter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a calorimeter module with a BGO pre-shower is a good choice.
this prototype module of the LHC hadron calorimeter is fully functional and meets the specifications.
the performance of the calorimeter is excellent and meets all requirements for the L3 detector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the calorimeter module is a viable detector for the L3 experiment at LEP.
the calorimeter module with BGO is an excellent prototype for the construction of the L3 uranium hadron calorimeter.
a gas sampling hadron calorimeter with a BGO pre-shower can be built with an energy resolution of about 17% for 20 GeV pions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BGO calorimeter is a good candidate for an L3 hadronic calorimeter.
the BGO calorimeter can be operated at the same voltage as the proportional chambers.
BGO can be successfully employed to improve the energy resolution of the L3 uranium hadron calorimeter module.
